html:
The Liberal Wars were a civil war in Portugal from 1828 to 1834 between liberals who wanted a constitutional monarchy and absolutists who wanted the king to rule alone.

After Brazil became independent under Pedro, the Portuguese heir, Pedro gave the Portuguese crown to his young daughter Maria with a constitution. His brother Miguel, regent for her, made himself absolute king in 1828. Pedro gave up the Brazilian throne in 1831 and came to fight. His forces held Porto through a long siege.

The liberals won in 1834 and Miguel went into exile. Maria II became queen. The church lost its monasteries, which were closed and sold. The war settled that Portugal would be a constitutional monarchy, until the republic of 1910. It followed the flight of the court to Brazil.
sum: The Liberal Wars were a civil war in Portugal from 1828 to 1834 between liberals who wanted a constitutional monarchy and absolutists who wanted the king to rule alone.
